clue.text: Impostor was plainly injured — moved awkwardly

parts.note: a sham is a fake, someone pretending to be what they are not
to bleed visibly is to be plainly hurt; past tense bled

explanation.surface: A fraud got visibly hurt and staggered off clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk with a clumsy, shuffling gait, so the past tense means moved awkwardly.

clue.text: Flag, which is quite normal

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a banner carried into battle and also means ordinary or usual.

clue.text: Mites bursting into song — could be a bloomer!

indicators.note: the rearranged mites go inside the word for song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: bursting suggests breaking apart, so the letters of mites are scattered

explanation.surface: Tiny insects burst into song, which might be a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, British slang for a gaffe, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic plants such as wormwood, so it may flower.

clue.text: Counsels person painting Scottish island

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers, legal counsel
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Lawyers and an artist on a Hebridean outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: The current's dropping

parts.note: read as news that an electric current or price is falling, but it describes sea water receding as the flow falls away

explanation.surface: A report that the electrical current is falling.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding flow of the sea after high water is a current that falls.

clue.text: Fool assumes it's wrong to offer help

indicators.note: the fool takes on the following letters, so they are attached after it

parts.note: an ass is a silly person

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of it's are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: An idiot wrongly presumes that it is a mistake to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IT'S into IST, which 'assumes' tacks onto ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to aid someone, which is offering help.

clue.text: Where to maintain sailing vessels — or just their spars?

definitions.meaning: places where boats are built and repaired
the yards of a ship, the spars that carry its sails

explanation.definitionFit: Docks for boat building, and read as two words, the yardarms belonging to a ship.

clue.text: Popular support's rising in the country

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for support is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aid is support; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Popular backing is growing in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AID into DIA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Man relinquishing capital to occupy lodge, possibly

definitions.text: Man relinquishing capital to occupy lodge, possibly

indicators.note: the shortened man is placed inside the lodge, as an occupant lives within

parts.note: a tent such as a wigwam is one kind of lodge

indicators.note: giving up the capital letter, so the first letter of man is dropped

parts.note: the word man spelt out

explanation.surface: A person giving up the city to live in a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodge, possibly' points at a wigwam-style dwelling; read whole, the clue also describes someone renting a home, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rents and lives in a dwelling, such as a lodge, is its occupant.

clue.text: A girl's embracing acceptable handsome youth

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the word for acceptable inside it

parts.note: Di is a girl's name; with the 's it gives DIS
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a suitable good-looking young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth, stands for any beautiful young man.

clue.text: Player about to appear in a top spot

indicators.note: the word for about is to be placed within the following words, so it shows up inside them

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop or peak
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A performer is about to turn up at a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky peak, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in the theatrical sense is a performer on stage.

clue.text: Pedagogue travelled on, in very poor health

parts.note: a teacher may hold a BEd, the Bachelor of Education degree, so is called one
a horse that has been travelled on has been ridden

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster went on a ride though gravely ill.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is the British teaching degree, Bachelor of Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed by illness is in very poor health.

clue.text: Denouncing the mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone is condemning their homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation, the act of denouncing someone utterly.

clue.text: Long period before noon

indicators.note: the period comes ahead of the letter for noon in the answer

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lengthy stretch of time ahead of midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the period; it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave it intensely, the same verb sense.

clue.text: One craft, in part, is producing food

indicators.note: one and craft are placed inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
I is the Roman numeral for one
SS is a steamship, a vessel or craft

explanation.surface: A single boat is said to be partly making a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat, a dish to eat.

clue.text: To throw money around wildly proves to have a limit

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of proves are thrown into a new order

parts.note: an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Spending recklessly turns out to have a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend too much is to splash cash about, a paraphrase.

clue.text: How to make note not sound abrasive

definitions.text: How to make note not sound abrasive

parts.words: How to make note not sound abrasive
parts.note: read as a musician's tip, but a grating bow drawn across a fiddle string produces a note that sounds rasping; the word for that action also means a harsh, abrasive noise

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a musical note from sounding harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as advice on a smooth tone; the answer is the very action that makes a fiddle note harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch a bow roughly over strings gives a rasping note, the opposite of a sweet sound.

clue.text: Top person here appears about the same

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for here goes round the same

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
id is short for idem, Latin for the same

explanation.surface: The boss in attendance looks much the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation, its leading figure.

clue.text: Attending the big match or he'll swear!

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A fan at the big game threatens to curse.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEST is an international cricket match, the biggest fixture in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestor is one who bears witness under oath, so someone who will swear.

clue.text: Gift of an ancient coin

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight and money in the ancient Greek and Hebrew world

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a natural aptitude and an old monetary unit of biblical times.

clue.text: Hold-up man gets very little money in European city

indicators.note: the money goes inside the city

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
P is a penny, a tiny amount of money

explanation.surface: A robber gets a tiny sum in a continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was a notorious English highwayman of the 1700s.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Turpin robbed coaches on the road, a highway robber who held people up.

clue.text: Insignificant person captures pawn, delivering check

indicators.note: the insignificant person holds the pawn within, as a chess piece is taken

parts.note: an insect is a contemptibly small, unimportant person
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A lowly chess player takes a pawn and announces check.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to examine it closely, a synonym.

clue.text: Aromatic stuff to cause arousal?

definitions.meaning: a gum or spice burned for its sweet smell
to enrage, stirring up strong feeling

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fragrant substance burned in worship; stressed on the second syllable, the verb means to make furious.

clue.text: Formal royal letters given academic introduction

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Stiff royal correspondence prefaces a scholarly work.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary textbook introducing a subject.

clue.text: Swindles involving many in strikes

indicators.note: the letter for many is placed inside the word for strikes

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or blows
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Frauds that implicate many people in industrial stoppages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests walkouts but means knocks. A RAMP is British slang for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramps in British slang are rackets or confidence tricks, so they are swindles.

clue.text: Hidden charges are lucrative sources

definitions.meaning: explosive devices buried out of sight
pits yielding profitable ore, or rich supplies of anything

explanation.definitionFit: The word means buried explosives and also rich pits of minerals, as in a gold seam.

clue.text: Eccentric once — tried to be obscure

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of the usual, so the letters of once and tried are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball once attempted to be enigmatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is little known and hard to grasp, so obscure.

clue.text: Bond in action (double O seven)

parts.note: reads as the spy agent 007 at work, but describes a tying loop, a bond doing its job, and the double O hints at the pair of letters at its heart

explanation.surface: James Bond, agent 007, on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points at the spy, but 'Bond' is a tie; a hangman's loop is a bond in action.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop that tightens is a working tie, a bond that grips.

clue.text: People secured backing for such inheritance laws

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective describing those laws of heredity

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: backing means the word for secured is read backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it firmly

explanation.surface: Men obtained support for certain laws of heredity.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel founded genetics, and his laws of heredity carry his name as an adjective.

clue.text: Plain where nothing green is to be found

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A flat landscape where nothing grows green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun, a flat landscape; it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and unconcealed, so plain to see.

clue.text: Stay in part of army camp

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a side is a faction or camp in a dispute

explanation.surface: Lodging in one section of a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell or live somewhere, so to stay.

clue.text: One doesn't like to take animals without examination

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the animals go round the examination

parts.note: deer are animals
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes taking animals without checking them first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater is someone who loathes things, the sense of one who doesn't like.
